ablation.kurz: Removal of material by laser irradiation.
ablation.definition: In laser ablation material is removed by evaporation, melt ejection, spallation or plasma processes. It sets in above the [[ablationsschwelle|ablation threshold]].
ablation.mehr: Put simply, ablation is “removing material with light”. Which mechanism dominates depends mainly on fluence and pulse duration: just above the threshold, thin layers are gently detached; at high fluence, vapour and droplets are ejected explosively. Compared with PBF-LB/M: there, evaporation is a nuisance (spatter, fumes); here, material ejection is the goal.

ablationsschwelle.kurz: Fluence above which material removal sets in (material specific).
ablationsschwelle.definition: The ablation threshold is the [[fluenz]] above which material removal sets in. It is material specific. Derivation and determination follow in chapter K07.
ablationsschwelle.mehr: Think of the threshold as a waterline: only the part of the beam profile above it removes material. That is why the crater of a Gaussian beam is smaller than the spot, and why small fluence changes near the threshold change the crater a lot. The threshold is not a fixed material constant: it depends on pulse duration, wavelength and number of pulses, among others ([[inkubation|incubation]]).

abschwaecher.kurz: Component for continuous adjustment of the pulse energy.
abschwaecher.definition: Common: a rotatable half-wave plate in front of a polarizer. The laser itself remains unchanged.

absorption.kurz: Uptake of light energy by the material.
absorption.definition: In absorption the light gives energy to the material (excitation of electrons or lattice vibrations). Together with [[reflexion]] and [[transmission]], $A+R+T=1$ holds.

absorptionskoeffizient.kurz: Attenuation of the intensity per path length, $\alpha$ in 1/m (or 1/cm).
absorptionskoeffizient.definition: The absorption coefficient $\alpha$ describes the attenuation in the Beer–Lambert law $I(z)=I_0e^{-\alpha z}$. Its inverse is the [[eindringtiefe|penetration depth]].
absorptionskoeffizient.mehr: The coefficient tells you which fraction of the intensity is lost per unit path length. Large $\alpha$: the energy stays in a thin surface layer (typical of metals). Small $\alpha$: light passes through the material (transparent glass). For ultrashort pulses on dielectrics, $\alpha$ is not constant but grows during the pulse as free electrons are generated.

abstract.kurz: Short summary of an article: aim, method, result, conclusion.
abstract.definition: The abstract decides whether you read an article. When reading, a good order is: abstract, figures, conclusion, then methods.

abtragrate.kurz: Removed volume per time, e.g. in mm³/min.
abtragrate.definition: The removal rate $\dot V$ follows from volume per pulse and repetition rate. Relative to the power one obtains the efficiency in mm³/(min·W).

autokorrelation.kurz: Pulse duration measurement in which the pulse is superimposed with a time-delayed copy of itself.
autokorrelation.definition: In an intensity autocorrelation a pulse is split, delayed in time and superimposed in a nonlinear crystal (SHG). The width of the signal over the delay is $\tau_\mathrm{AC}=\kappa\,\tau$, with $\kappa=\sqrt2$ for Gaussian pulses. The pulse shape has to be assumed.
autokorrelation.mehr: The problem: no detector is fast enough to resolve a fs pulse directly. The trick: the pulse is measured with itself. The SHG signal only appears when both copies overlap in time; scanning the delay of one copy samples the pulse duration. Drawback: the trace is always symmetric and says nothing about the chirp. You therefore have to assume a pulse shape to convert the width into a pulse duration.

avalanche-ionisation.kurz: Avalanche-like multiplication of free charge carriers.
avalanche-ionisation.definition: In avalanche ionization a free electron absorbs laser energy and creates further free electrons by collision, so that their number grows like an avalanche. Seed electrons come e.g. from [[multiphotonenabsorption]].
avalanche-ionisation.mehr: Like a snowball triggering an avalanche: a free electron gains energy in the laser field (it absorbs photons as a free carrier) until it has enough energy to free a second electron from the valence band by impact. Both repeat this, so the number of electrons grows exponentially. The avalanche needs seed electrons and some time; its share is therefore larger for longer pulses, while multiphoton ionization contributes more for very short pulses.

axicon.kurz: Conical optical element that generates a Bessel beam.
axicon.definition: An axicon produces a long, narrow focal line with which glass can be modified through its full thickness.

bandluecke.kurz: Energy range without electron states between valence and conduction band, $E_\mathrm{g}$.
bandluecke.definition: The band gap $E_\mathrm{g}$ separates the valence band from the conduction band. Photons with less energy cannot excite the material through a single absorption; dielectrics are therefore transparent in the visible and near infrared. Metals have no band gap.
bandluecke.mehr: Picture: the valence band is a fully occupied parking deck, the conduction band an empty deck above it, and in between there are no parking spaces. An electron can only move up if it receives enough energy at once. A single photon with too little energy does not help, no matter how many photons arrive; only at very high intensity can several photons act simultaneously. That is why the band gap is the key quantity for understanding USP ablation of glass, ceramics and semiconductors.

bessel-strahl.kurz: Beam shaping for cutting glass through the full thickness.
bessel-strahl.definition: Bessel beam and filamentation are beam-shaping concepts with which glass can be cut through its full thickness.
bessel-strahl.mehr: An [[axicon]] makes the beam converge in a cone; the partial beams interfere along the axis over a long distance. This creates a long, thin focal line instead of a short focal spot. A single shot can thus modify a channel through the full glass thickness, ideal for glass cutting. Filamentation achieves something similar through a balance of self-focusing and defocusing by the plasma.

beugung.kurz: Spreading of waves around obstacles and through apertures; limits the focus size.
beugung.definition: Because of diffraction light cannot be focused arbitrarily sharply; the smallest focus is of the order of the wavelength. Diffraction-limited means $M^2\approx1$.
beugung.mehr: Every limitation of a wave makes it spread. That is why you cannot focus arbitrarily small: the smallest focus is of the order of the wavelength. Smaller spots need a shorter wavelength or a larger numerical aperture (larger beam on the lens, shorter focal length).

bpp.kurz: Product of waist radius and divergence half-angle, $\mathrm{BPP}=w_0\theta=M^2\lambda/\pi$.
bpp.definition: The beam parameter product $\mathrm{BPP}=w_0\theta$ is conserved in lossless beam shaping with ideal optics and characterizes the beam quality. For the ideal Gaussian beam $\mathrm{BPP}=\lambda/\pi$. Usual unit: mm·mrad.
bpp.mehr: The BPP behaves like a conserved quantity of optics: with lenses you can shrink the focus, but then the divergence grows and the product stays the same. A poor beam cannot be improved with optics, at most by filtering at the cost of power.

brechungsindex.kurz: Ratio of the vacuum speed of light to the phase velocity in the material, $n=c/v$.
brechungsindex.definition: The refractive index $n$ determines how strongly light is refracted and delayed in the material. Together with the extinction coefficient $\kappa$ it forms the complex refractive index $\tilde n=n+\mathrm{i}\kappa$. It depends on the wavelength ([[dispersion]]).
brechungsindex.mehr: Inside a material the light wave travels more slowly; the frequency stays the same, so the wavelength becomes shorter. This leads to refraction at interfaces, to reflection (Fresnel) and, because $n$ depends on wavelength, to dispersion, which stretches ultrashort pulses in time. The imaginary part $\kappa$ describes absorption.

brennweite.kurz: Distance between lens and focus for parallel incident light, $f$.
brennweite.definition: The focal length $f$ determines, together with wavelength, $M^2$ and beam radius on the lens, the focus size: $w_0\approx M^2\lambda f/(\pi w_\mathrm{in})$.

bruchzaehigkeit.kurz: Resistance of a material to crack propagation, $K_\mathrm{Ic}$.
bruchzaehigkeit.definition: The fracture toughness $K_\mathrm{Ic}$ (unit MPa√m) states at which stress intensity an existing crack grows unstably. Ceramics have low values, metals high ones.

burst-mode.kurz: Pulse packets instead of single pulses.
burst-mode.definition: In burst mode, pulse packets are emitted instead of single pulses, with pulse spacings down to the GHz range. According to the project notes this increases removal rate and efficiency.
burst-mode.mehr: Instead of one large pulse, the energy is split into several closely spaced sub-pulses. Each sub-pulse is closer to the most favourable fluence, and later sub-pulses hit material that is still excited or warm from the previous one. Whether this improves removal rate and quality depends strongly on material, number of sub-pulses and their spacing; the literature is not uniform here.

chirp.kurz: Change of the instantaneous frequency within a pulse over time.
chirp.definition: A pulse is chirped if its instantaneous frequency rises or falls along the pulse, e.g. after dispersion. At the same bandwidth a chirped pulse is longer than the Fourier-limited pulse.
chirp.mehr: The name comes from birdsong: a tone whose pitch changes. After normal glass, the red (long-wavelength) part leads and the blue part trails, because red light travels faster there (positive chirp). The spectrum stays the same; only the colours are sorted in time. CPA exploits exactly this: chirp on purpose (stretch), amplify, then remove the chirp (compress).

coulomb-explosion.kurz: Ions are repelled from a positively charged surface and ejected.
coulomb-explosion.definition: When many electrons leave the surface it stays positively charged; the electrostatic repulsion can eject ions and small clusters. Discussed for dielectrics and semiconductors near the threshold.
coulomb-explosion.mehr: Sequence: the laser removes many electrons from the surface within a short time. In dielectrics and semiconductors, electrons do not flow back fast enough (unlike in a metal), so the surface layer stays positively charged. Like-charged ions repel each other and the layer “explodes” electrostatically. This would be a particularly gentle removal of very thin layers near the threshold; how important it is in practice is debated in the literature.

cpa.kurz: Amplification of stretched pulses, the basis of all high-power UKP systems.
cpa.definition: In chirped pulse amplification (CPA) the pulse is stretched in time, amplified and compressed again. According to the project notes it is the basis of all high-power UKP systems. Details follow in chapter K04.
cpa.mehr: The basic problem: a high-energy fs pulse would reach such a high peak intensity in the amplifier that the crystal or fibre would be damaged by self-focusing and other nonlinear effects. The trick: stretch the pulse in time by orders of magnitude, which lowers the peak power by the same ratio, amplify it safely, and compress it again at the end. Picture: you carry a bulky piece of furniture through a narrow door in parts and reassemble it on the other side.

d2-methode.kurz: Determining threshold and beam radius from the square of the crater diameter versus $\ln E_\mathrm{p}$.
d2-methode.definition: According to Liu (1982), $D^2=2w_0^2\ln(E_\mathrm{p}/E_\mathrm{th})$. A straight line in the $D^2$–$\ln E_\mathrm{p}$ diagram gives $w_0$ from the slope and the threshold energy from the zero crossing.
d2-methode.mehr: Why $D^2$ versus $\ln E_\mathrm{p}$? The Gaussian beam decays exponentially towards the edge, and the crater rim lies where the local fluence just reaches the threshold. Taking the logarithm turns the exponential into a straight line. In practice: make craters at several pulse energies, measure the diameters, plot $D^2$ against $\ln E_\mathrm{p}$ and fit a line. The slope gives the beam radius, the intercept with $D^2=0$ the threshold energy. A nearly Gaussian profile is required.

debris.kurz: Redeposited ablation material around the processed spot.
debris.definition: Debris consists of particles, droplets and condensate. It degrades edge quality and roughness and is reduced by extraction or shielding gas.

dielektrikum.kurz: Electrical insulator with a large band gap, usually transparent in the visible.
dielektrikum.definition: Dielectrics such as fused silica and sapphire absorb light in the visible and near infrared only through nonlinear processes. That makes volume processing possible.
dielektrikum.mehr: The most important change of mindset compared with metals: a dielectric has practically no free electrons. The laser first has to create them itself (multiphoton and avalanche ionization) before significant energy is absorbed. That is why everything depends on intensity here.

diffusionslaenge.kurz: Distance that heat travels in the time $\tau$, $L_\mathrm{th}\approx\sqrt{D\tau}$.
diffusionslaenge.definition: If $L_\mathrm{th}$ is smaller than the [[eindringtiefe|penetration depth]], the energy stays in the absorption volume: hardly any heat-affected zone.
diffusionslaenge.mehr: Rule of thumb: in the time $\tau$, heat travels about $\sqrt{D\tau}$. Because of the square root, a pulse 1000 times shorter gives a diffusion length about 30 times smaller. Compare $L_\mathrm{th}$ with the penetration depth: if $L_\mathrm{th}$ is smaller, the energy stays where it was absorbed during the pulse.

dispersion.kurz: Dependence of the refractive index on wavelength, which stretches pulses in time.
dispersion.definition: Because of dispersion, different frequency components of a pulse travel at different speeds. The group delay dispersion (GDD, $\varphi_2$ in fs²) describes the second-order effect. Positive GDD stretches a pulse, negative GDD can shorten it again.
dispersion.mehr: An ultrashort pulse is not single-coloured light but a whole spectrum, and the shorter the pulse, the broader the spectrum. If the colours travel at different speeds in a material, they no longer arrive together: the pulse becomes longer and chirped. Every lens, window and crystal in the beam path contributes. That is why the pulse on the workpiece can be longer than directly at the laser output.

divergenz.kurz: Widening of the beam with distance, half-angle $\theta$.
divergenz.definition: The divergence of a Gaussian beam is $\theta=M^2\lambda/(\pi w_0)$. A small focus means large divergence.

doe-element.kurz: Optic that shapes or splits the beam by diffraction.
doe-element.definition: DOEs produce e.g. top-hat profiles or several beams for parallel processing.

doi.kurz: Persistent identifier of an article, resolvable via doi.org.
doi.definition: A DOI has the form 10.xxxx/yyyy. It should be in every literature entry and is the most reliable way to find an article again.

eigenspannung.kurz: Mechanical stress in a component without external load.
eigenspannung.definition: Residual stresses arise e.g. from non-uniform heating and cooling or from local modification (volume change). In glass and ceramics they can trigger cracks.

eindringtiefe.kurz: Depth at which the intensity has dropped to $1/e$, $\delta=1/\alpha$.
eindringtiefe.definition: The (optical) penetration depth $\delta=1/\alpha$ determines in which layer the energy is absorbed. A small $\delta$ means high energy density and a low threshold.
eindringtiefe.mehr: The penetration depth is the thickness of the layer in which most of the energy ends up: down to the depth $\delta$, about 63 % has been absorbed ($1-1/e$). The thinner this layer, the higher the energy density there and the lower the fluence needed for ablation. In dielectrics the optical penetration depth is initially very large (transparent); only the generated free electrons make it small during the pulse.

elektron-phonon-kopplung.kurz: Energy transfer from the electrons to the lattice, constant $G$.
elektron-phonon-kopplung.definition: The coupling determines how fast the electron and lattice systems equalize (time scale of a few picoseconds). It enters the two-temperature model as $G(T_\mathrm{e}-T_\mathrm{l})$.
elektron-phonon-kopplung.mehr: The electrons absorb the laser energy first and become very hot while the atoms (the lattice) are still cold. The coupling is the “heat exchanger” between the two: through collisions, the electrons give off energy as lattice vibrations ([[phonon|phonons]]). If the pulse is shorter than this transfer time, it is over before the lattice heats up. That is the core reason why ultrashort pulses act differently from ns pulses.

f-theta.kurz: Scan lens in which the position is proportional to the deflection angle, $x=f\theta$.
f-theta.definition: The f-theta lens focuses onto a flat field and fixes focus size and working field (both $\propto f$).
f-theta.mehr: An ordinary lens focuses obliquely incident beams onto a curved surface, and the spot position grows with $\tan\theta$. The f-theta lens is corrected so that the focus stays in a plane and the position grows linearly with the mirror angle. A scanner turning at constant angular speed therefore produces a constant track speed on the workpiece.

faserlaser.kurz: Laser with a doped glass fibre as the gain medium.
faserlaser.definition: Fibre lasers are compact, robust and easy to cool; the high intensity in the small fibre core limits the pulse energy through nonlinearities.

fluenz.kurz: Pulse energy per area in J/cm², central process quantity.
fluenz.definition: The fluence $F=E_\mathrm{p}/A$ is the pulse energy delivered per area, here in J/cm². It is the central process quantity; ablation sets in above the [[ablationsschwelle]]. For a [[gauss-strahl]] one distinguishes the peak fluence $F_0$ from the mean fluence.
fluenz.mehr: The difference from your previous world: in PBF-LB/M you think in energy per length or volume over many micro- to milliseconds. With ultrashort pulses, what counts is the energy per area in a single pulse: “How much energy hits one square centimetre in one shot?” Be careful with values in papers: the peak fluence $F_0=2E_\mathrm{p}/(\pi w_0^2)$ is twice the average fluence $E_\mathrm{p}/(\pi w_0^2)$; always check which one is meant.

fokuslage.kurz: Position of the focus relative to the workpiece surface.
fokuslage.definition: The focus position $z$ is a process parameter of its own: even small deviations change the peak fluence. In depth ablation it is tracked.

fourier-limit.kurz: Shortest pulse duration for a given spectrum, without chirp.
fourier-limit.definition: A transform-limited pulse satisfies $\tau\Delta\nu=K$. Any chirp makes the pulse longer.
fourier-limit.mehr: The shorter a pulse, the broader its spectrum must be (Fourier transform). Conversely, a given spectrum sets a minimum duration. A transform-limited pulse uses its spectrum optimally: all colours arrive at the same time. Any chirp makes it longer.

frequenz.definition: The frequency $\nu$ states how often the light wave oscillates per second. For light of 1030 nm, $\nu=c/\lambda\approx2.9\cdot10^{14}\,\mathrm{Hz}$. Do not confuse it with the repetition rate of a laser.

fresnel.kurz: Reflectance and transmittance at an interface, depending on angle and polarization.
fresnel.definition: The Fresnel equations give reflection and transmission at the interface of two media, depending on the angle of incidence, the [[polarisation|polarization]] and the (complex) [[brechungsindex|refractive index]].
fresnel.mehr: How much light is lost at the surface depends on angle and polarization. At oblique incidence, p-polarized light (field in the plane of incidence) is reflected less than s-polarized light, and on transparent media not at all at Brewster's angle. This matters as soon as the beam hits inclined surfaces, for example steep crater walls or during drilling.

frog.kurz: Method for reconstructing the amplitude and phase of a pulse.
frog.definition: FROG measures a spectrogram (spectrally resolved autocorrelation) and provides pulse shape and chirp, unlike plain [[autokorrelation|autocorrelation]].
frog.mehr: An autocorrelation only gives a width. FROG additionally resolves the signal spectrally: a spectrum is recorded for every delay. From this 2D image (spectrogram) an algorithm reconstructs intensity and phase of the pulse, and hence also the chirp.

galvo-scanner.kurz: Two fast mirrors that deflect the beam.
galvo-scanner.definition: Together with an [[f-theta]] lens it reaches scan speeds in the m/s range. Inertia and acceleration limit the contour accuracy.

gauss-strahl.kurz: Beam with a Gaussian intensity profile, described by the beam radius $w_0$.
gauss-strahl.definition: A Gaussian beam has the radial intensity profile $I(r)=I_0\,e^{-2r^2/w_0^2}$. The [[strahlradius]] $w_0$ is the radius at which the intensity has dropped to $1/e^2$ of the maximum.
gauss-strahl.mehr: Almost all ultrashort-pulse lasers deliver an approximately Gaussian beam. The profile matters because the fluence in the centre is twice the average fluence and falls off quickly towards the edge. The beam therefore removes material deeply in the centre and not at all at the edge, and the crater is smaller than the spot. A Gaussian beam stays Gaussian when focused; only its size changes.

gdd.definition: The GDD $\varphi_2$ describes how the group delay changes with frequency. It determines how strongly a pulse is stretched in time by a material.
gdd.mehr: GDD measures how strongly an optical element stretches a pulse; the values add up along the beam path. Short pulses are more sensitive: the same GDD lengthens a pulse with a broad spectrum (short pulse) much more than one with a narrow spectrum (longer pulse).

gitter.kurz: Periodic arrangement of the atoms in a solid.
gitter.definition: In the two-temperature model “lattice” stands for the system of atomic cores and their vibrations ([[phonon|phonons]]), as opposed to the electron system.

halbleiter.kurz: Material with a small band gap; conductivity between metal and insulator.
halbleiter.definition: In semiconductors the ratio of photon energy to band gap decides whether absorption is linear. Examples: silicon, silicon carbide.
halbleiter.mehr: For semiconductors, the wavelength decides which regime you get: if the photon energy is above the band gap, the material absorbs linearly; if it is below, the material is transparent and can only be processed nonlinearly. The same material can therefore respond very differently at 515 nm and at 2 µm.

halbwertsbreite.kurz: Width of a curve at half of its maximum value.
halbwertsbreite.definition: The full width at half maximum (FWHM) is the full width of a distribution at half height. For pulses the FWHM of the intensity is usually given, for the beam diameter often the $1/e^2$ diameter. For a Gaussian profile $d_\mathrm{FWHM}=w\sqrt{2\ln2}\approx1.18\,w$.

hatch.kurz: Distance between adjacent scan tracks in area ablation.
hatch.definition: The hatch $h$ is the spacing of the scan lines in area ablation. Together with the pulse spacing it determines the pulse number per area, the accumulated fluence and the area rate $\dot A=v\,h$.
hatch.mehr: As in PBF-LB/M, tracks lie side by side at a distance $h$. With ultrashort pulses the hatch is chosen smaller than the spot diameter so that the tracks overlap and the floor becomes flat. Too large a hatch leaves grooves; too small a hatch costs time and adds heat.

haz.kurz: Edge region altered by heat; minimal with UKP.
haz.definition: The heat-affected zone (HAZ) is the region next to the processed spot whose microstructure or properties were changed by heat. With UKP it is considered minimal.
haz.mehr: In metals, the HAZ shows up as microstructural change, temper colours or a melt rim; in glass and ceramics rather as microcracks, stresses or a changed refractive index. “Minimal” does not mean zero: at high repetition rates or with many pulses, a measurable HAZ can form even with ultrashort pulses.

inkubation.kurz: Lowering of the ablation threshold by preceding pulses.
inkubation.definition: In the incubation effect the [[ablationsschwelle]] falls when the same spot has already been hit by earlier pulses.
inkubation.mehr: Every pulse below the threshold leaves small traces: defects, colour centres, stresses or surface changes. They make absorption easier for the next pulse. Consequence: when many pulses hit the same spot, the threshold drops and approaches a limiting value. Important in practice: when scanning, every spot is hit by many pulses, so the multi-pulse threshold is what matters, not the single-pulse threshold.

intensitaet.kurz: Power per area in W/cm²; for pulses approximately $F/\tau$.
intensitaet.definition: The intensity $I$ is the power per area (here W/cm²). For a pulse $I\approx F/\tau$ holds approximately. Nonlinear effects such as [[multiphotonenabsorption]] depend on the intensity, not on the fluence.
intensitaet.mehr: Fluence tells you how much energy arrives, intensity how fast it arrives. At the same fluence, a pulse that is a hundred times shorter has a hundred times the intensity. For transparent materials this is decisive, because nonlinear absorption grows with a high power of the intensity, not with the fluence.

interferenz.kurz: Superposition of waves: reinforcement or cancellation depending on phase.
interferenz.definition: Interference arises when coherent waves are superimposed. Examples in laser processing: autocorrelation, [[lipss]] and diffractive optics.

ionisation.kurz: Release of electrons from bound states.
ionisation.definition: In a dielectric ionization means the excitation of an electron from the [[valenzband|valence band]] into the [[leitungsband|conduction band]]. Mechanisms: multiphoton, tunnel and impact ionization.

keldysh-parameter.kurz: Number $\gamma$ that distinguishes multiphoton ($\gamma\gg1$) from tunnel ionization ($\gamma\ll1$).
keldysh-parameter.definition: The Keldysh parameter $\gamma$ compares the laser frequency with the tunnelling frequency of an electron in the deformed potential barrier. For $\gamma\gg1$ multiphoton ionization dominates, for $\gamma\ll1$ tunnel ionization. The transition region lies at $\gamma$ close to $1$ to $2$.
keldysh-parameter.mehr: Two pictures of the same ionization: in a weaker, rapidly oscillating field, the electron “collects” several photons at once (multiphoton, large $\gamma$). In a very strong field, the potential barrier is bent so far that the electron can tunnel through before the field reverses (tunnelling, small $\gamma$). $\gamma$ decreases with increasing intensity and with longer wavelength.

keramik.kurz: Inorganic, non-metallic, mostly polycrystalline and brittle material.
keramik.definition: Technical ceramics (e.g. aluminium oxide, silicon nitride) are hard, wear-resistant and temperature-resistant, but [[spoedigkeit|brittle]] and sensitive to [[thermoschock|thermal shock]].

knife-edge.kurz: Beam radius measurement by moving an edge through the beam.
knife-edge.definition: The radius follows from the transmitted power: $w=\Delta x_{10\text{–}90}/1.28$ for a Gaussian beam.

kohaerenz.kurz: Fixed phase relationship of the light wave over time (temporal) or space (spatial).
kohaerenz.definition: Laser light is coherent: the phases are correlated over large distances. This enables sharp focusing and interference.
kohaerenz.mehr: Temporal coherence describes how long a wave stays “in step”, spatial coherence over which cross-section. Laser light is highly coherent, which is why it can be focused to a diffraction-limited spot and can form interference patterns. A light bulb cannot do this.

kollimation.definition: A collimated beam has an almost constant radius over a long distance. Before focusing, the beam is usually collimated and expanded.

kompressor.kurz: Dispersive arrangement with negative GDD that shortens the pulse again.
kompressor.definition: Usually a grating pair. The compressor has to cancel the total dispersion of the system; it is often placed behind the amplifier.
kompressor.mehr: The compressor is the mirror image of the [[strecker|stretcher]]: usually two gratings are arranged so that the leading colours travel a longer path and the trailing ones catch up. It has to compensate the total GDD of the system. A misaligned compressor is a common cause of pulses that are too long on the workpiece.

krater.kurz: Depression that one or several pulses leave in the material.
krater.definition: The crater diameter $D$ is used in the [[d2-methode|D² method]] to determine threshold and beam radius.

kritische-dichte.kurz: Electron density at which the plasma frequency equals the laser frequency: $n_\mathrm{c}=\varepsilon_0m_\mathrm{e}\omega^2/e^2$.
kritische-dichte.definition: When a plasma reaches the critical density $n_\mathrm{c}$, it shields the laser light and absorbs or reflects strongly. For $\lambda=1030\,\mathrm{nm}$, $n_\mathrm{c}\approx1\cdot10^{21}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$.
kritische-dichte.mehr: As long as there are few free electrons, light can enter the material. As the electron density grows, the natural frequency of the electron gas increases. Above the critical density it follows the light field and screens it like a metal: the light is reflected or strongly absorbed. Reaching the critical density is therefore often used as a criterion for breakdown or damage in dielectrics. It scales with $1/\lambda^2$.

lambert-beer.kurz: Exponential decay of the intensity in the material, $I=I_0e^{-\alpha z}$.
lambert-beer.definition: The Beer–Lambert law describes linear absorption: the intensity falls exponentially with the depth $z$. It no longer holds for nonlinear absorption, because $\alpha$ then depends on the intensity.
lambert-beer.mehr: Each layer attenuates the light by the same fraction, not by the same amount; this gives the exponential decay. On a semi-log plot it is a straight line with slope $-\alpha$. For ultrashort pulses in glass the law does not hold during the pulse, because $\alpha$ itself grows with intensity.

laser.kurz: Light source that produces coherent light by stimulated emission.
laser.definition: Laser stands for light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation. A gain medium in a [[resonator]] produces coherent, usually narrow-band light with low divergence.

leitungsband.kurz: Energetically higher electron band, empty in the ground state (insulator, semiconductor).
leitungsband.definition: Electrons in the conduction band are mobile and absorb light as free carriers. In metals the conduction band is partly filled.

lipss.kurz: Self-organized periodic nanostructures on the surface.
lipss.definition: LIPSS (laser-induced periodic surface structures) are self-organized, periodic nanostructures that form on the surface under laser irradiation.
lipss.mehr: LIPSS form when the incident light interferes with light scattered at the surface or with excited surface waves. This creates a periodic energy pattern that is imprinted over many pulses. Roughly, one distinguishes structures with a period close to the wavelength (LSFL) and much finer ones (HSFL). Their orientation follows the polarization. Use: functional surfaces (wetting, friction, colour). Nuisance: unwanted roughness on the crater floor.

m2.kurz: Measure of beam quality: $M^2=1$ is ideally Gaussian, larger values focus worse.
m2.definition: The beam propagation factor $M^2\ge1$ is the ratio of the beam parameter product (BPP) of a real beam to that of the ideal Gaussian beam. It is determined according to ISO 11146 from the second moments of the intensity distribution. A high $M^2$ enlarges the focus or shrinks the Rayleigh length for the same optics.
m2.mehr: $M^2$ tells you how much worse a real beam can be focused than an ideal Gaussian beam. With the same optics, the focal radius grows by a factor of $M^2$; if you keep the focal radius the same instead, the Rayleigh length shrinks by $M^2$. For ablation this means: a high $M^2$ costs peak fluence or depth of focus.

messunsicherheit.kurz: Range in which the true value of a measured quantity is expected.
messunsicherheit.definition: Uncorrelated relative uncertainties are added in quadrature. For the fluence the beam radius enters twice: $\delta F/F=\sqrt{(\delta E/E)^2+(2\delta w/w)^2}$.

mittlere-leistung.definition: The average power $P_\mathrm{avg}=E_\mathrm{p}\cdot f$ is pulse energy times repetition rate. It determines the heat load and the throughput, not the peak load on the material.
mittlere-leistung.mehr: The number on the data sheet (say “50 W”) is almost always the average power. It determines how much material you can remove per unit time and how much heat is generated overall. For the effect of a single pulse, pulse energy and fluence are what matter.

modenkopplung.kurz: Fixed phase locking of the cavity modes, so that a short pulse circulates in the cavity.
modenkopplung.definition: In mode locking all longitudinal cavity modes oscillate with a fixed phase relationship. Their superposition is a pulse that passes through the cavity with the round-trip time $2L/c$. The more modes (bandwidth), the shorter the pulse.
modenkopplung.mehr: A laser cavity can support many frequencies (modes) at the same time. If they oscillate with random phases, the result is a noisy continuous signal. If the phases are locked, the modes add up constructively only once per round trip: a short pulse forms that travels back and forth in the cavity and releases a part at the output coupler on every round trip. Picture: many runners who all cross the finish line at exactly the same moment.

multiphotonenabsorption.kurz: Simultaneous absorption of several photons in transparent media.
multiphotonenabsorption.definition: In multiphoton absorption several photons take up energy at the same time, although each single [[photonenenergie|photon]] has too little energy for the band gap. It is a nonlinear process and only relevant at high [[intensitaet]] (Keldysh theory).
multiphotonenabsorption.mehr: Why “simultaneous”? There is no intermediate state in the band gap where the electron could wait. The photons have to arrive within an extremely short time, and the probability of that grows with $I^{\,n}$. Two important consequences: absorption only happens where the intensity is highest (in the focus), and glass can be processed inside without touching the surface.

nichtthermischer-abtrag.kurz: Ablation where the energy reaches the lattice before heat can flow away.
nichtthermischer-abtrag.definition: “Non-thermal” is a limiting case: even with UKP the energy ends up as heat, but the heat-affected zone stays small because there is no time for diffusion.
nichtthermischer-abtrag.mehr: The term is misleading: it does not mean “cold” but “faster than heat conduction”. The energy is deposited and the material removed so quickly that hardly any heat flows into the surrounding material. With many pulses at a high rate, heat can still build up ([[waermeakkumulation|heat accumulation]]).

oszillator.kurz: Mode-locked laser that produces the short seed pulse.
oszillator.definition: The oscillator delivers pulses in the nanojoule range at a high rate (e.g. 100 MHz). It is the first building block of a [[cpa]] system.

peer-review.kurz: Expert evaluation of a manuscript by independent specialists before publication.
peer-review.definition: Peer review safeguards the quality of scientific articles but does not guarantee correctness. Preprints are not peer reviewed.

phasenexplosion.kurz: Sudden decay of superheated melt into vapour and droplets.
phasenexplosion.definition: In a phase explosion (explosive boiling) the melt is superheated to temperatures near the critical temperature and decays into a mixture of vapour and droplets. Typical at fluences well above the threshold.
phasenexplosion.mehr: Normal boiling needs time for bubbles to form. With ultrashort pulses, the surface layer is heated so quickly that it becomes superheated far above the boiling point without boiling. Close to the critical temperature the liquid suddenly decomposes into vapour and droplets. This explains the strong material ejection at high fluences.

phonon.definition: Phonons are the quasi-particles of lattice vibrations. Hot electrons give energy to the lattice via [[elektron-phonon-kopplung|electron–phonon coupling]].
phonon.mehr: The atoms in a crystal behave like balls connected by springs and vibrate together in waves. A phonon is the smallest packet of this vibrational energy. “Lattice temperature” intuitively means how strongly these vibrations are excited.

photon.definition: A photon is the energy quantum of light. It carries the energy $h\nu=hc/\lambda$ and the momentum $p=h/\lambda$.

photonenenergie.definition: A photon of wavelength $\lambda$ carries the energy $h\nu=hc/\lambda\approx 1239.84\ \mathrm{eV\,nm}/\lambda$. Whether a single photon can bridge the band gap of a material decides between linear and [[multiphotonenabsorption]].
photonenenergie.mehr: The rule of thumb $E\,[\mathrm{eV}]\approx1240/\lambda\,[\mathrm{nm}]$ is the most important number for absorption questions: compare it with the band gap. A shorter wavelength means more energy per photon and fewer photons to bridge the band gap. Higher intensity does not change the energy of a photon, only the number of photons.

plasma.kurz: Ionized gas or electron gas of high density that behaves like a metal.
plasma.definition: At high electron density (after multiphoton ionization and avalanche) the excited material behaves like a plasma: it absorbs and reflects light differently from the starting material.
plasma.mehr: When so many electrons are free that they move collectively, the material behaves optically like a metal. Important for the process: a plasma or ablation plume above the surface or in the crater can shield subsequent light, especially at high repetition rates and in burst mode.

plasmafrequenz.kurz: Natural frequency of the electron gas, $\omega_\mathrm{p}^2=n_\mathrm{e}e^2/(\varepsilon_0m_\mathrm{e})$.
plasmafrequenz.definition: Below the plasma frequency a plasma reflects, above it it is transparent. Equality with the laser frequency defines the [[kritische-dichte|critical density]].
plasmafrequenz.mehr: Picture: the electron gas is a mass–spring system. When displaced, it oscillates back at $\omega_\mathrm{p}$. If the light oscillates more slowly ($\omega<\omega_\mathrm{p}$), the electrons follow the field and reflect it. If it oscillates faster, they cannot keep up and the light passes through.

polarisation.kurz: Direction of oscillation of the electric field of the light wave.
polarisation.definition: Polarization can be linear, circular or elliptical. It affects absorption at oblique incidence and the orientation of [[lipss]].
polarisation.mehr: For processing, polarization matters in two places: on inclined surfaces (crater walls, holes), p- and s-polarized light are absorbed differently, and LIPSS align with it. For drilling, circular polarization is therefore often used to obtain round, direction-independent results.

preprint.kurz: Manuscript before or without peer review, e.g. on arXiv.
preprint.definition: Preprints are available early but not peer reviewed. If possible cite the peer-reviewed version.

pulsabstand.kurz: Distance between two consecutive pulses on the workpiece, $d=v/f$.
pulsabstand.definition: The pulse spacing $d=v/f$ follows from scan speed $v$ and repetition rate $f$. Compared with the spot diameter $2w_0$ it determines the pulse overlap.

pulsdauer.kurz: Temporal width of the pulse (usually full width at half maximum), symbol $\tau$.
pulsdauer.definition: The pulse duration $\tau$ is the temporal width of a pulse, usually given as the full width at half maximum (FWHM).

pulsenergie.kurz: Energy of a single laser pulse, symbol $E_\mathrm{p}$, in joules.
pulsenergie.definition: The pulse energy $E_\mathrm{p}$ is the energy of a single pulse, measured in joules (usually microjoules in UKP systems). Together with [[pulsdauer]] and [[repetitionsrate]] it fixes [[spitzenleistung]] and [[mittlere-leistung]].

pulspicker.kurz: Switch that selects individual pulses from the pulse train.
pulspicker.definition: With an acousto-optic or electro-optic modulator the repetition rate of the oscillator is lowered to the process rate, or bursts are formed.

pulszug.definition: A pulse train has the average power $E_\mathrm{p}f$ and the much higher peak power $E_\mathrm{p}/\tau$.

quarzglas.definition: Fused silica is transparent from UV to near infrared and has a very low thermal expansion. It is the standard material for volume processing with fs pulses and for [[sle]].

rauheit.kurz: Short-wavelength deviation of the surface from the ideal shape, e.g. $Ra$ or $Sa$.
rauheit.definition: Profile parameters ($R$) are in ISO 21920, areal ones ($S$) in ISO 25178. Without stating filters, roughness values are not comparable.

rayleighlaenge.kurz: Distance from the focus after which the beam cross-section doubles: $z_\mathrm{R}=\pi w_0^2/(M^2\lambda)$.
rayleighlaenge.definition: The Rayleigh length $z_\mathrm{R}$ is the distance from the beam waist at which the beam radius has grown to $\sqrt2\,w_0$ (cross-section area doubled, peak fluence halved). It determines the depth of focus: $z_\mathrm{R}=\pi w_0^2/(M^2\lambda)$.
rayleighlaenge.mehr: The Rayleigh length measures the tolerance along the beam axis: within $\pm z_\mathrm{R}$ the beam stays almost the same size. A small focus means a short Rayleigh length, quadratically: if you halve $w_0$, $z_\mathrm{R}$ drops to a quarter. With small spots the focus position therefore has to be set very precisely and tracked during deep ablation.

reflexion.kurz: Return of a fraction of the light at the surface, reflectance $R$.
reflexion.definition: At normal incidence on a transparent medium of refractive index $n$ the reflectance is $R=((n-1)/(n+1))^2$. Metals reflect considerably more.

repetitionsrate.kurz: Pulses per second in hertz, symbol $f$.
repetitionsrate.definition: The repetition rate $f$ states how many pulses are emitted per second. The pulse spacing is $1/f$; the [[mittlere-leistung]] is $E_\mathrm{p}\cdot f$.
repetitionsrate.mehr: A higher rate means more pulses per second and thus more throughput, but also less time to cool down between pulses. At fixed average power, the pulse energy drops as the rate increases. And the scanner has to move faster to keep the same pulse spacing.

resonator.kurz: Arrangement of mirrors in which the light circulates and is amplified.
resonator.definition: The cavity fixes the allowed modes. For a linear cavity of length $L$ the mode spacing is $c/(2L)$.

rissbildung.kurz: Formation of cracks by thermal or mechanical stresses.
rissbildung.definition: In laser ablation of brittle materials cracks arise from steep temperature gradients, residual stresses or pressure waves. Countermeasures: lower fluence, less heat accumulation, adapted scan strategy.

saphir.kurz: Single-crystal aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃), hard and transparent.
saphir.definition: Sapphire is a very hard, transparent single crystal used as window and substrate material; processing it is demanding because of its hardness and brittleness.

schaerfentiefe.kurz: Axial region around the focus with almost unchanged fluence, about $2z_\mathrm{R}$.
schaerfentiefe.definition: The depth of focus of the focus is of the order of $2z_\mathrm{R}$. It shrinks with the square of the focus radius.

scheibenlaser.kurz: Solid-state laser with a thin crystal disk as the gain medium.
scheibenlaser.definition: The thin disk is cooled over its large area; this allows high average power with good beam quality.

selbstfokussierung.kurz: The Kerr effect focuses an intense beam above a critical power.
selbstfokussierung.definition: The intensity is higher in the beam centre, and so is the refractive index: the medium acts like a lens. Self-focusing can destroy amplifier media and is the basis of filamentation.
selbstfokussierung.mehr: The refractive index increases slightly with intensity (Kerr effect). The intensity is highest in the centre of the beam, so $n$ is too: the material acts like a converging lens and focuses the beam further, which raises the intensity even more. Above a critical power this effect wins against diffraction. It can destroy optics, but it is used deliberately to create filaments.

selbstphasenmodulation.kurz: An intensity-dependent refractive index broadens the spectrum of a pulse.
selbstphasenmodulation.definition: Through the Kerr effect ($n=n_0+n_2I$) an intense pulse changes its own phase. This generates new frequencies and limits the pulse energy in amplifiers.
selbstphasenmodulation.mehr: An intense pulse changes the refractive index in step with its own intensity. Its phase therefore shifts with time, new frequencies appear on the edges, and the spectrum broadens. In an amplifier this degrades pulse quality; in pulse-compression stages it is used deliberately to broaden the spectrum for even shorter pulses.

shg.kurz: Nonlinear process that doubles the frequency and halves the wavelength.
shg.definition: In a nonlinear crystal two photons of the fundamental become one of double the energy: 1030 nm becomes 515 nm. It is also the basis of [[autokorrelation|autocorrelation]].
shg.mehr: A strong light field drives the electrons in the crystal into nonlinear oscillations, which also produces light at twice the frequency. This only works efficiently if the fundamental and the harmonic stay in step inside the crystal (phase matching); crystal angle or temperature therefore have to be right. For processing, green light means a smaller focus and different absorption than the fundamental.

silizium.kurz: Elemental semiconductor with an indirect band gap, standard material of microelectronics.
silizium.definition: Silicon absorbs at photon energies above the band gap and is largely transparent below it. Wafers are thinned and structured with UKP lasers.

sle.kurz: fs modification in the volume plus wet-chemical etching.
sle.definition: In selective laser etching (SLE) the material is first modified with femtosecond pulses and then etched wet-chemically; mainly in fused silica.
sle.mehr: Two steps that you can optimize separately: the laser changes the glass in the focus so that it etches faster, without removing material yet. The etching bath then preferentially removes the modified regions. Advantages over direct ablation: no debris, hardly any cracks, internal channels and undercuts are possible. Important: every modified region must be connected to the surface, otherwise the etchant cannot reach it.

slm.kurz: Liquid-crystal display that shapes the phase of the beam position-dependently.
slm.definition: With an SLM, beam profiles and multiple foci can be programmed dynamically.

spallation.kurz: Layer-by-layer flaking by tensile stress after fast energy deposition.
spallation.definition: In spallation the ultrafast energy deposition creates a pressure wave that is reflected as a tensile wave and detaches material layer by layer. It is mainly discussed near the ablation threshold.
spallation.mehr: Intuitively: an ultrashort pulse heats a thin layer so quickly that it cannot expand in time, which creates a high pressure. The pressure wave travels into the material, a tensile wave forms at the surface, and if the tensile stress exceeds the strength, a layer spalls off. Similar to a hard blow on a plate that makes material flake off on the back side.

spider.kurz: Interferometric method for measuring pulse shape and phase.
spider.definition: SPIDER reconstructs the spectral phase directly from an interferogram and is suited for very short pulses.

spitzenleistung.kurz: Maximum optical power during the pulse, approximately $E_\mathrm{p}/\tau$.
spitzenleistung.definition: The peak power $P_\mathrm{peak}$ is the power at the maximum of the pulse. Approximately $P_\mathrm{peak}\approx E_\mathrm{p}/\tau$ holds; a pulse-shape factor of order 1 is neglected.
spitzenleistung.mehr: The same energy in a shorter time means higher power. A 10 µJ pulse lasting 1 ps already has a peak power of about 10 MW, even though the average power of the laser may be only a few watts. Peak power governs nonlinear effects (self-focusing, multiphoton absorption); average power governs heat and throughput.

spoedigkeit.definition: Brittle materials such as glass and ceramics fail suddenly under tensile stress through crack propagation. That limits the permissible thermal and mechanical load in laser ablation.

spotdurchmesser.kurz: Diameter of the beam in the focus, usually $2w_0$ (at $1/e^2$).
spotdurchmesser.definition: The spot size is not equal to the ablated diameter: because of the threshold the crater is smaller than $2w_0$.

strahlaufweiter.kurz: Telescope that enlarges the beam radius.
strahlaufweiter.definition: A larger beam on the lens gives a smaller focus ($w_0\propto1/w_\mathrm{in}$).

strahlprofil.kurz: Spatial distribution of the intensity across the beam.
strahlprofil.definition: The beam profile is determined with a camera or the knife-edge method. Typical profiles: Gaussian, top-hat, Bessel.

strahlradius.kurz: Radius $w_0$ at which the intensity has dropped to $1/e^2$.
strahlradius.definition: The beam radius $w_0$ (based on the $1/e^2$ criterion) is the distance from the beam axis at which the intensity has dropped to $1/e^2\approx 13.5\,\%$ of the maximum. In the focus it is the focus radius.

strahltaille.kurz: Narrowest point of the beam (focus) with radius $w_0$.
strahltaille.definition: At the beam waist the wavefront is flat and the peak fluence is maximal. From there the beam widens with the [[rayleighlaenge|Rayleigh length]] as the length scale.
strahltaille.mehr: At the waist the wavefronts are flat; before and after it they are curved. For processing, it is the reference point of the focus position: “focus on the surface” means the waist lies in the workpiece plane. Because the radius is smallest there, the peak fluence is highest there.

strecker.kurz: Dispersive arrangement that lengthens the pulse in time.
strecker.definition: The stretcher produces positive [[gdd]] and lowers the peak power before the amplifier by the stretch factor.
strecker.mehr: In the stretcher, different colours travel paths of different length (e.g. via gratings or in a long fibre): one side of the spectrum arrives first, the other later. The pulse thus becomes longer by orders of magnitude and its peak power correspondingly smaller. The [[kompressor|compressor]] reverses this at the end.

tastverhaeltnis.kurz: Fraction of time in which power flows, $\tau\cdot f$.
tastverhaeltnis.definition: For UKP lasers the duty cycle is tiny (e.g. $3\cdot10^{-8}$ at 300 fs and 100 kHz). It is the ratio of average to peak power.

temperaturleitfaehigkeit.kurz: Measure of how fast temperature equalizes, $D=\lambda_\mathrm{th}/(\rho c_p)$.
temperaturleitfaehigkeit.definition: The thermal diffusivity $D$ (unit m²/s) determines the [[diffusionslaenge|diffusion length]] $L_\mathrm{th}\approx\sqrt{D\tau}$.
temperaturleitfaehigkeit.mehr: Thermal conductivity alone does not tell you how fast a temperature profile spreads; it also depends on how much heat the material stores. $D$ combines both. High $D$ (metals): heat spreads quickly. Low $D$ (e.g. glass): heat stays local, creating steep temperature gradients and hence stresses.

thermalisierung.kurz: Establishment of an equilibrium distribution of the excited electrons.
thermalisierung.definition: After excitation the electrons share their energy among themselves. Only then is an electron temperature $T_\mathrm{e}$ defined.
thermalisierung.mehr: Right after absorption, individual electrons have very different energies; one cannot yet speak of a temperature. Through collisions with each other they share the energy until an equilibrium distribution forms. Only then is the electron temperature in the [[ttm|TTM]] well defined.

thermoschock.kurz: Cracking caused by rapid temperature changes.
thermoschock.definition: Rapid heating creates a temperature gradient and thus thermal stress. If it exceeds the strength, the component fractures. Thermal shock resistance depends on expansion, conduction and strength.
thermoschock.mehr: If a surface is heated quickly, it wants to expand while the cooler material below holds it back, which creates stresses. Brittle materials cannot relieve them by plastic flow, so a crack forms. A single ultrashort pulse is less critical, but heat accumulation at high repetition rates can make thermal shock relevant again.

thg.kurz: Generation of the third harmonic: wavelength divided by three.
thg.definition: From 1030 nm one obtains about 343 nm. A shorter wavelength means a smaller focus and fewer photons needed for the band gap.

ti-saphir.kurz: Solid-state laser with a very large gain bandwidth around 800 nm.
ti-saphir.definition: Because of the large bandwidth pulses of a few femtoseconds are possible. Kerr-lens mode locking is common.

transmission.kurz: Passage of light through the material.
transmission.definition: The transmission $T$ is the fraction of light that passes through the material. Transparent dielectrics have a high transmission at photon energies below the band gap.

ttm.kurz: Model with separate temperatures for electron and lattice systems.
ttm.definition: The two-temperature model (TTM) describes the electron and lattice systems with separate temperatures that exchange energy through a coupling. It is the standard model for the interaction of ultrashort pulses with metals.
ttm.mehr: Why two temperatures? Right after the pulse the electrons are extremely hot while the ion cores are still cold; there is no common temperature. The TTM describes both systems with their own heat equations, coupled through $G(T_\mathrm{e}-T_\mathrm{l})$. After a few picoseconds both have equilibrated. For dielectrics the model has to be extended, because the free electrons first have to be generated.

ueberlapp.kurz: Fraction of the spot diameter that consecutive pulses cover jointly.
ueberlapp.definition: The linear overlap $O=1-d/(2w_0)$ describes how far consecutive spots lie on top of each other. High overlap means many pulses per spot and thus incubation and heat accumulation.
ueberlapp.mehr: At 0 % the spots just touch. At 90 % each pulse moves on by only a tenth of the diameter, so every point on the line is hit by about ten pulses. Overlap is the lever with which you control the number of pulses per spot, incubation and heat accumulation. Careful: some papers calculate it with the crater diameter instead of $2w_0$.

ukp.kurz: Laser pulse in the picosecond to femtosecond range.
ukp.definition: An ultrashort pulse (UKP, USP) has a duration in the picosecond to femtosecond range. The energy enters the material faster than heat can flow away (see [[ttm]]).
ukp.mehr: Where “ultrashort” begins is not sharply defined. What matters is the comparison with the time scales in the material: if the pulse is shorter than electron–lattice coupling and heat conduction, the process works in a fundamentally different way. That is why pico- and femtosecond pulses differ strongly or hardly at all, depending on the material.

valenzband.kurz: Energetically low electron band that is filled at $T=0$.
valenzband.definition: The valence band holds the electrons involved in bonding. An excitation into the [[leitungsband|conduction band]] requires at least the energy of the [[bandluecke|band gap]].

verstaerker.kurz: Stage that raises the pulse energy to micro- to millijoules.
verstaerker.definition: Types: regenerative and multipass amplifiers, fibre amplifiers, thin-disk lasers. In [[cpa]] the amplifier sees the stretched pulse.

verstaerkungsmedium.kurz: Material that amplifies light by stimulated emission.
verstaerkungsmedium.definition: Examples: ytterbium-doped crystals and fibres (around 1030 nm) and titanium–sapphire (around 800 nm). The bandwidth of the medium limits the shortest pulse duration.

versuchsplanung.kurz: Systematic planning of experiments to gain a lot of information with few runs.
versuchsplanung.definition: Typical designs: factorial ($2^k$), central composite (CCD), Box–Behnken. Replicates, randomization and centre points secure the conclusions.

volumenmodifikation.kurz: Local change of the material in the interior by focused fs pulses.
volumenmodifikation.definition: In transparent materials the focus changes density, refractive index or etchability without damaging the surface. Applications: [[sle]], [[wellenleiter|waveguides]], markings.
volumenmodifikation.mehr: Because absorption is nonlinear, it only happens in the focus; the glass in front and behind remains untouched. Depending on the pulse energy, smooth refractive-index changes (waveguides), nanoscale gratings (readily etchable, the basis of [[sle|SLE]]) or voids form. This is a unique feature of ultrashort-pulse processing of transparent materials.

waermeakkumulation.kurz: Rise of the temperature from pulse to pulse at a high rate.
waermeakkumulation.definition: Heat accumulation occurs when the pulse spacing is shorter than the cooling time. It enlarges the heat-affected zone and can promote melt and cracks.
waermeakkumulation.mehr: Picture: water drips into a bucket with a hole. If the drops (pulses) arrive more slowly than the bucket drains (heat flows away), it stays empty. If they arrive faster, the level (temperature) rises from pulse to pulse. At high repetition rates and large overlap, many “cold” single pulses thus add up to a thermal process.

wellenlaenge.kurz: Spatial distance between two equal wave phases, $\lambda=c/\nu$.
wellenlaenge.definition: The wavelength $\lambda$ is the distance between two consecutive wave crests. It is linked to the frequency by $\lambda=c/\nu$. Typical UKP wavelengths: 1030 nm (fundamental), 515 nm (SHG), 343 nm (THG).

wellenleiter.kurz: Structure with raised refractive index that guides light.
wellenleiter.definition: With fs pulses waveguides can be written directly into glass by leaving a track of slightly raised refractive index with the focus.

zeit-bandbreite-produkt.definition: Pulse duration and spectral width are coupled through the Fourier transform: $\tau\,\Delta\nu\ge K$, where $K$ depends on the pulse shape (Gaussian: $0.441$; sech²: $0.315$). Equality holds for Fourier-limited pulses without chirp.
zeit-bandbreite-produkt.mehr: This is, so to speak, the uncertainty relation of optics: a short event needs many frequencies. In practice you use the measured pulse duration and spectrum to check whether the pulse is well compressed. If $\tau\Delta\nu$ is clearly above $K$, the pulse still carries a chirp.

zerstoerschwelle.kurz: Fluence above which an optic or sample is permanently damaged.
zerstoerschwelle.definition: Test methods such as 1-on-1 and S-on-1 are given in ISO 21254. The LIDT depends on pulse duration, wavelength and pulse number.
zerstoerschwelle.mehr: The LIDT is the counterpart of the ablation threshold for optics: this is how far you may load them, with a safety margin. Be careful when comparing: values only apply to a specific pulse duration, wavelength and number of pulses; with many pulses the threshold is often lower ([[inkubation|incubation]]).

packaging.kurz: Everything that turns a chip into a usable component.
packaging.definition: Packaging (German: Aufbau- und Verbindungstechnik, AVT) connects the chip electrically, fans out the contact pitch, removes heat, protects it and makes it handleable and testable.

back-end.kurz: Manufacturing steps after the wafer fab: thinning, singulating, assembling, connecting, encapsulating, testing.
back-end.definition: The back end follows wafer manufacturing (front end). Not to be confused with the [[beol]], the on-chip wiring made in the fab.

beol.kurz: Metallization levels on the chip, made in the fab.
beol.definition: The BEOL comprises the copper lines and vias above the transistors, embedded in dielectrics such as [[low-k]]. Despite its name it belongs to the front end.

wafer.kurz: Thin disc of semiconductor material on which many chips are made at once.
wafer.definition: Chips are made on the wafer in the front end; in the back end it is thinned and singulated into individual [[die|dies]].

die.definition: A die is a chip after singulation, still without a package. Plural: dies.

ritzgraben.kurz: Narrow area between the chips where separation takes place.
ritzgraben.definition: The dicing street (scribe line) often contains test structures of metal and dielectric. Its width co-determines how many chips fit on a wafer.

kerf.kurz: Width removed by the separation process.
kerf.definition: In sawing the kerf is about as wide as the blade; stealth dicing creates practically none. Narrow kerfs allow narrow streets and more chips per wafer.

dicing.kurz: Separating the wafer into individual chips.
dicing.definition: Processes: wafer saw, [[laser-grooving]] plus saw or plasma, [[stealth-dicing]], laser full cut, [[plasma-dicing]].

low-k.kurz: Insulator with low permittivity between the lines of the chip.
low-k.definition: Low-k materials lower line capacitance and thus RC delay and energy. Many are porous and mechanically weak; they delaminate easily during sawing.

drahtbonden.kurz: Connecting the chip pads with thin wires by ultrasound, heat and force.
drahtbonden.definition: In wire bonding the active side faces up and the pads sit at the chip edge. The number of connections grows only with the perimeter.

flip-chip.kurz: Chip is soldered face down with bumps across its area.
flip-chip.definition: Flip chip allows many connections in an area array and short paths. The gap is filled with [[underfill]].

bump.kurz: Small solder or copper contact on the chip for flip-chip connections.
bump.definition: Bumps are applied on the wafer. Variants: solder balls, copper pillars with solder cap, microbumps for chip stacks.

underfill.kurz: Filled epoxy in the gap between flip chip and substrate.
underfill.definition: The underfill couples chip and substrate mechanically and relieves the solder joints from shear caused by different thermal expansion.

moldmasse.kurz: Epoxy with silicon dioxide filler for encapsulating chips.
moldmasse.definition: Mould compound protects the chip and forms the reconstituted wafer in fan-out. For the laser it is a composite of polymer and transparent filler.

bga.kurz: Package with solder balls in an area array on its underside.
bga.definition: The BGA connects a package to the circuit board. In FCBGA a flip chip sits on an IC substrate with a BGA.

ic-substrat.kurz: Mini circuit board between chip and board, made of core and build-up layers.
ic-substrat.definition: The IC substrate translates the fine chip pitch to the board pitch. Its build-up layers of [[abf|ABF]] and copper are connected by [[microvia|microvias]].

abf.kurz: Filled epoxy dielectric of the build-up layers of IC substrates.
abf.definition: ABF (Ajinomoto Build-up Film) is laminated, cured and drilled with microvias. The high silicon dioxide filler content lowers thermal expansion.

microvia.kurz: Small, mostly laser-drilled blind hole through one build-up layer.
microvia.definition: A microvia connects two neighbouring layers of a substrate. Quality features: diameter, [[taper]], wall, clean bottom, intact copper pad.

rdl.kurz: Fine copper wiring in polymer at wafer or panel level.
rdl.definition: The RDL routes connections from the chip to the solder balls, in [[wlp]] and [[fan-out]] with lithographic processes.

wlp.kurz: Packaging all chips at once on the wafer, before singulation.
wlp.definition: In fan-in (WLCSP) the package stays as large as the chip; in [[fan-out]] the area is extended by mould compound.

fan-out.kurz: Wafer-level package whose redistribution extends beyond the chip edge.
fan-out.definition: Chips are embedded with spacing in mould compound; chip-first or chip-last (RDL-first) on temporary carriers, often released by [[laser-debonding]].

interposer.kurz: Wiring carrier on which several chips sit side by side (2.5D).
interposer.definition: Interposers are made of silicon with [[tsv|TSVs]], of organic material or of glass with [[tgv|TGVs]].

tsv.definition: TSVs connect stacked chips or the top and bottom of a silicon interposer.

tgv.kurz: Through-via in glass, e.g. in glass core substrates or glass interposers.
tgv.definition: TGVs are mostly made with lasers: by [[lide|laser-induced etching]] or direct ultrashort pulse drilling. Microcracks and residual stresses are critical.

glaskern-substrat.kurz: IC substrate with a core of glass instead of glass-fibre-reinforced epoxy.
glaskern-substrat.definition: Named advantages are thermal expansion closer to silicon, flatness and high hole density; the challenge is crack-free drilling of the [[tgv|TGVs]].

hybrid-bonding.kurz: Direct bonding of copper to copper and dielectric to dielectric, without solder.
hybrid-bonding.definition: Hybrid bonding allows very tight pitches for chip stacks. It requires extremely clean, flat surfaces and therefore low-particle separation processes.

chiplet.kurz: Small partial chip of a system that is tightly connected with others in the package.
chiplet.definition: Chiplets improve yield and allow different process nodes; they are connected via interposers, bridges or stacks.

osat.kurz: Service provider for semiconductor assembly and test.
osat.definition: OSATs take over the [[back-end]] for chip makers and foundries.

cte.kurz: Relative change in length per kelvin, $\alpha$ in 1/K.
cte.definition: Different CTEs of joined materials create stresses, solder joint shear and [[verzug|warpage]].

verzug.kurz: Bending of a package or wafer due to different thermal expansion.
verzug.definition: Warpage complicates soldering and bonding; it is a main problem for moulded wafers and large substrates.

chipping.kurz: Shell-shaped breakouts at chip or glass edges.
chipping.definition: Chipping arises when separating brittle materials and lowers the [[die-festigkeit|die strength]]. Front-side and back-side chipping are distinguished.

die-festigkeit.kurz: Fracture strength of a singulated chip, determined by edge flaws.
die-festigkeit.definition: Measured in the three-point bending test (SEMI G86) or ring-on-ring, evaluated according to [[weibull]]. The separation process influences it strongly.

weibull.kurz: Statistics of the strength of brittle materials according to the weakest link.
weibull.definition: $P_\mathrm{f}=1-\exp[-(\sigma/\sigma_0)^m]$ with characteristic strength $\sigma_0$ and Weibull modulus $m$ (scatter).

laser-grooving.kurz: Opening the layer stack in the dicing street with the laser before separation.
laser-grooving.definition: The laser removes low-k, metal and passivation; afterwards a saw or a plasma separates the silicon. Ultrashort pulses reduce the heat input.

stealth-dicing.kurz: Laser modifies the interior of a wafer, separation by stretching the tape.
stealth-dicing.definition: At a wavelength at which silicon is largely transparent, a modified layer forms only in the focus. Dry, no debris, hardly any kerf.

plasma-dicing.kurz: Dry etching of all dicing streets at the same time.
plasma-dicing.definition: Plasma dicing avoids mechanical and thermal edge damage but needs metal-free streets and a clean mask; often combined with [[laser-grooving]].

dbg.kurz: First groove or modify, then thin until the chips separate.
dbg.definition: In DBG and the laser variant SDBG, backgrinding completes the separation. This protects thin chips.

rueckduennen.kurz: Grinding the wafer from the back side to the target thickness.
rueckduennen.definition: Thin wafers allow thin packages and stacks but are more fragile.

laser-debonding.kurz: Releasing a glass carrier by laser irradiation of a release layer.
laser-debonding.definition: A UV laser irradiates through the transparent carrier; the release layer decomposes above a threshold and the carrier releases with low force.

lide.kurz: Laser modifies glass, then hydrofluoric acid preferentially etches the track.
lide.definition: Related to [[sle|SLE]]: an ultrashort pulse modifies the glass through its thickness; the etching time determines the diameter of the [[tgv|TGV]].

taper.kurz: Narrowing of a hole from top to bottom.
taper.definition: Usually given as diameter ratio $d_\mathrm{bot}/d_\mathrm{top}$ or as wall angle; the definition differs between papers.

top-hat.kurz: Beam profile with nearly constant intensity and steep flanks.
top-hat.definition: A top-hat profile is created with refractive or diffractive beam shapers; in drilling it gives steeper walls than a Gaussian beam.

perkussionsbohren.kurz: Drilling with many pulses on the same spot.
perkussionsbohren.definition: In percussion drilling, focus and fluence set the diameter. It is distinct from [[trepanieren|trepanning]] (cutting out a contour) and [[wendelbohren|helical drilling]] (many circular revolutions into depth).

csam.kurz: Non-destructive imaging of delamination and voids with ultrasound.
csam.definition: Ultrasound is strongly reflected at interfaces with an air gap; delaminations in the package thus become visible.

querschliff.kurz: Prepared section through a sample for examination under the microscope.
querschliff.definition: Cross-sections show via profiles, interfaces, voids and taper; they are destructive.

trepanieren.kurz: Drilling by cutting out a circular contour; the core drops out.
trepanieren.definition: The beam follows a circular path and cuts through the contour. The diameter follows from the path, not the focus. Some papers also use the term for [[wendelbohren|helical drilling]].

wendelbohren.kurz: Drilling with many circular revolutions, layer by layer into depth.
wendelbohren.definition: The beam circles many times and removes material layer by layer, often with a rotating optic that also sets the angle of incidence. Gives round, precise holes with adjustable [[taper|taper]], but is slower than [[perkussionsbohren|percussion drilling]].

aspektverhaeltnis.kurz: Ratio of depth to diameter of a hole or trench.
aspektverhaeltnis.definition: A high aspect ratio means deep, narrow structures. It limits how well the beam reaches and particles leave the hole bottom, and how well the hole can be measured from above.

lsm.kurz: Confocal microscope that scans a surface point by point and delivers 3D topography.
lsm.definition: Delivers height maps for diameter, depth, profile and [[rauheit|roughness]]. Steep walls and deep, narrow holes give hardly any signal; with transparent samples, reflections from the rear side can interfere.

rem.kurz: Microscope that scans the surface with an electron beam; high magnification and depth of field.
rem.definition: Shows cracks, [[debris|debris]], melt and [[lipss|LIPSS]] in detail. Non-conductive samples (glass, polymer) charge up and are coated with a thin conductive layer or examined in low vacuum.
